methods: Independent source review of shared candidate/admin monthly reservations, settlement, router bounds, quotas, billing boundary and admin budget display.
Read supplied live-service-baseline.json and root-budget-reconciliation.json only; no independent production query.

Local mocked tests: npx vitest run --config supabase/tests/vitest.backend.config.ts supabase/tests/jobvance-openrouter.test.ts supabase/tests/jobvance-admin.test.ts --maxWorkers=4; 2 files, 19 tests passed.
Official OpenRouter usage-accounting and Supabase cost-control documentation checked 2026-10-14; no current model prices assumed.
not_tested: No invoices, payouts, payments, keys, private account records or new paid model/search calls accessed.
No independent hosted interaction or live concurrency test.
No merchant eligibility, paid subscription lifecycle, actual full operating expense or support time verified.

criteria.name: Shared expenditure containment
criteria.evidence: Candidate reservation migration 20261012181402 lines106-125 and admin platform lines108-148 share locked monthly ledger. Supplied $0.740100 aggregate reconciles.

criteria.name: Settlement and reconciliation operations
criteria.evidence: Conservative retained uncertainty and idempotent settlement exist; supported admin actions do not provide reconciliation; supplied aggregate has $0.225976 uncertain.

criteria.name: Pilot allocation and quota discipline
criteria.evidence: Ten seats, three daily new runs, thirty scheduled monthly runs and two packs/run; no per-account dollar allocation or monthly admin allocation observed.

criteria.name: Unit cost and full operating expense visibility
criteria.evidence: AdminFounder shows processing categories, not useful-pack cost, all-in infrastructure expense or founder/support time.

criteria.name: Commercial boundary and future billing readiness
criteria.evidence: Proposals explicitly non-billing; core.ts:90 disables checkout unless enabled; current ten-pack pass does not implement proposed monthly subscriptions.

strengths: Shared candidate/admin lock enforces a maximum $50 UTC-month reservation ceiling; cap can be lowered.
Unknown costs retain reservations; settled calls release only reserved-minus-actual and settlement is idempotent.
Supplied ledger reconciles: 0.740100=0.002344+0.511780+0.225976; amounts are application-metered, not invoice verified.
Dashboard separates actual, reserved, uncertain, candidate and admin categories and explains QA/erasure limitations.
Free pilot and future price proposals are distinguished; no revenue or willingness-to-pay inferred.

findings.problem: Held usage has no explicit operator resolution workflow or aging owner.

evidence.detail: One admin operation retains $0.225976 uncertain; actual remains unknown.
Supported actions include snapshot/config/support/provider status, with no reconciliation action.
Manual invoice instruction references candidate usage tables, omitting admin table.
Official documentation supports asynchronous usage lookup using a generation ID, if retained.

findings.recommendation: Create a manual-first both-table reconciliation register with age, owner, held amount, available provider reference, evidence and next review; retain unverifiable holds.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture settlement updates monthly commitment exactly once.
Repeated resolution is harmless; missing provider evidence never releases a hold.
Month-end register covers candidate and admin operations, including no-reference uncertainty.
dependencies: Named operator; future authorized access to provider aggregate usage, outside this audit.
findings.cost_effect: Small operator effort; releases capacity only after evidenced settlement.

findings.problem: Count limits do not allocate the shared dollars among pilot accounts and admin work.

evidence.detail: New-run limit is three per account per UTC day.
Scheduled limits are one daily and thirty monthly.
Admin enforces batch cap alongside global cap; monthly pool allocation is absent.

findings.recommendation: Test provisional participant/admin allocations and per-account soft warnings under the existing atomic $50 cap; treat allocation as a hypothesis.
acceptance_criteria: Mixed-account/admin fixture respects selected allocations and $50 global ceiling.
Owner reallocations are explicit and audited.
dependencies: Observed route/use patterns; chosen fair-use policy.
findings.cost_effect: Redistributes availability without raising expenditure ceiling.

findings.problem: Processing totals cannot explain cost per useful approved/downloaded packet or assisted completion.

evidence.detail: Cost aggregates separate settled actual, reserved and uncertain; no useful-packet cohort cost.
Candidate erasure can remove details while committed ledger stays authoritative.

findings.recommendation: Use privacy-preserving monthly totals plus a pilot worksheet connecting completed/approved/downloaded outcomes, route, failures and assistance minutes, with denominator/erasure caveats.
acceptance_criteria: Ten fictional journeys including failure/erasure produce explainable operational totals.
No generated packet counted as submitted.
QA/admin costs separated; no candidate text retained for finance.
findings.cost_effect: Modest weekly review cost; provides evidence for later price/allowance decisions.

findings.problem: The $50 processing limit is clear, but no consolidated infrastructure and founder-time envelope is supplied.

evidence.detail: Ceiling excludes unrelated services, taxes and domain renewals.
Daily owner support review is expected without a time budget.
Actual infrastructure/renewal amounts and founder support hours were not accessed.
Supabase documents that its spend cap covers selected usage items, distinct from an application ledger.

findings.recommendation: Maintain a dated owner-held expense/time worksheet, marking actual versus assumptions and renewal/review thresholds; make no service purchase.
acceptance_criteria: Each service has an owner, amount or unknown marker and review/renewal date.
Track onboarding/support/operations hours separately from processing cash.
Scenario: ten users, twenty runs, two calls/run; assumed $0.03/$0.10 call gives $12/$40 candidate cost; $5 admin + $5 uncertainty gives $22/$50 committed, excluding paid search.
Founder scenario: 7.5h onboarding +10h support +4h operations=21.5h; assumed $30/h opportunity cost=$645; no profit forecast.
dependencies: Owner-supplied aggregate expenses and time observations.
findings.cost_effect: Reveals cost outside processing ceiling; no infrastructure upgrade recommended.

findings.problem: Proposed subscription allowances are not implemented by existing one-time ten-pack payment contract; this is deliberate deferral.

evidence.detail: $15/20 packs and $29/30 runs/60 packs marked not ready and billing false.
Existing purchase control is Buy ten packs.
Billing configuration disabled unless explicit enabled flag.

findings.recommendation: Keep checkout off; create a future commercial specification and lifecycle test gate only when paid scope is authorized. Respect deferred licence/permit decision.
acceptance_criteria: Future fixtures cover renewal/reset, cancellation, failed renewal, duplicate events, refunds and ledger reconciliation.
Commercial scope and provider/merchant setup confirmed before any future activation.
dependencies: Future paid scope authorization; selected entitlements; eligible merchant setup; no legal work or activation now.
findings.cost_effect: No current revenue; future payment processing/support costs remain unknown.

open_questions: Who owns weekly and UTC-month-close reconciliation across both candidate and admin usage?
What is the owner-approved cash envelope outside the AI/search cap and the available weekly support time?
What share of packets are approved/downloaded and reused for a second actual application, and at what assistance cost?
Which provisional allocation keeps one participant/admin batch from consuming other participants' access?
do_not_build_now: No paid checkout activation, licence/permit workaround or new legal advice.
No annual contracts, unlimited AI promises, paid acquisition or standalone finance platform.
No margin/profit projection from tiny metered sample or proposed $15/$29 prices.
